cohort: The study included 141 women with term prolonged rupture of membranes (>18h) and intrapartum fever, where 79 received ampicillin alone and 62 received ampicillin and gentamicin.
finding: Treatment with ampicillin alone compared to dual therapy (ampicillin and gentamicin) in women with prolonged ROM and fever was associated with higher rates of endometritis, neonatal early-onset sepsis, Enterobacteriaceae positive placental swab culture, and histopathological subchorionitis, suggesting it promotes ampicillin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae growth and increases infectious morbidity.
